title: Use your Android phone as a Google TV remote: setup and limits
description: Pair the Google TV app with your TV using its on-screen code, check the controls that work, and understand where The Remote's Android app fits.
body:
# Use your Android phone as a Google TV remote: setup and limits

Use the Google TV Android app on the TV’s home Wi-Fi, select your Android TV or Google TV, then pair with its on-screen code. [Google's Android TV remote guide](https://support.google.com/androidtv/answer/6122465?hl=en)

Before putting the physical remote away, try navigation, typing and the sound controls you use most.

## Check the device behind the screen

Here, **Google TV app** means the app on your phone. **Google TV device** means the TV or streaming device you want to control.

Find the model in the device's settings, manual, or product label and look up the manufacturer's platform specification. A brand name alone isn't a compatibility check. If an HDMI-connected box supplies your TV interface, identify that box too.

Google's remote instructions cover Android TV and Google TV. Its streaming-device instructions specifically include Chromecast with Google TV and Google TV Streamer. Don't extend that list to every device with Chromecast or Android in its name. [Google's streaming-device remote guide](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/11221499?hl=en)

Keep the TV switched on and, for a separate streamer, select its HDMI input. You need to see the pairing code.

If the TV is brand new or still connected to an old network, finish its setup first. Some Google TV models offer a phone-assisted initial setup, but the supported route varies. Follow the screen and the manufacturer's instructions rather than expecting the virtual remote to fix an unconfigured connection. [Google TV initial setup options](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/10050221?hl=en)

## Pair the Google TV app

Install or update [Google TV from Google LLC on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.videos&hl=en). The listing will show whether it's available for your phone and region.

For this Wi-Fi walkthrough, confirm that the phone and TV use the same home network. Open the TV's network settings to check; working internet on each device isn't enough to verify the local connection. [Google's virtual-remote network check](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/15766805?hl=en)

1. Open the Google TV app on your Android phone
2. Tap the TV connection button near the bottom-right of the app. Google's pages use **Connect TV** or a nearby-TV count for this entry point
3. Choose the TV or streamer you intend to control
4. Copy the pairing code from that TV screen into the phone app
5. Tap **Pair**, then try moving the selection on the TV

These are Google's documented steps. The connection-button wording varies across its help pages, so use the TV connection entry point visible in your version. [Google TV pairing instructions](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/11136134?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en)

If several devices appear, check the selected name before entering a code. If none appears, compare the network connections before starting over. If the app rejects the code, check the screen again rather than reusing one from a previous attempt.

## Check the controls you'll actually use

Google describes navigation, media playback, and phone-keyboard input among the virtual remote's functions. Use a short check on your setup before assuming every TV app behaves alike. [Google's description of basic controls](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/11221499?hl=en)

**Navigation:** Move between a few items, open one, then return with Back or Home. Watch the TV so you know you're controlling the intended device.

**Typing:** Open the search field you want to use and try a harmless phrase. Check that the right text reaches the right field. If navigation works but typing fails in one app, keep that distinction when troubleshooting.

**Playback:** Try pause and resume in the app you normally watch. Check each player you use regularly.

**Sound:** Check volume at a comfortable level. Note which device produces it: the TV, a soundbar, or a receiver.

Keep the original remote within reach for any controls that don't respond.

## Where the limits matter

### Volume and power depend on the setup

A physical streaming-device remote can control equipment through a different path from a phone app. Google documents infrared behavior for its Voice Remotes and separate volume settings for the streamer, TV, and external audio equipment. If phone navigation works but volume doesn't, investigate that audio path before pairing everything again. [Voice Remote control paths](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/12934376?hl=en), [Google's volume setup](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/10094150?hl=en)

### Remote control and casting do different jobs

The virtual remote sends control actions. Casting chooses media for a compatible receiver; [screen mirroring displays the phone's screen](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/6059461?hl=en). Choose the route that matches what you want to put on the screen. [Google TV remote and casting instructions](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/11136134?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en)

### A phone remote still needs a reachable device

The same-network setup described here isn't an away-from-home control service. A hotel or guest network may also block communication between connected devices. Ask the network owner about supported access instead of changing security settings at random. [Google's streaming-device network limitations](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/7566322?hl=en-CA)

## Where The Remote fits

The Remote is a separate, free Android phone app. It's built for compatible Android TV and Google TV devices on your home network, with Android TV Remote Service v2 required. Available controls vary by model.

You can enter a YouTube search on your phone, review a shared YouTube link before sending it, name saved TVs by room, and choose app-specific controls. YouTube behavior also depends on the TV and its YouTube version. [See The Remote's features and requirements](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/)

[Download the app](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#download) on your Android phone. It's free, with no ads and no account. Before installing, check that your TV is compatible and on the same home network as your phone.
summary: Pair your phone and check the controls you actually use.

title: Android TV remote app can't find your TV? Start here
description: TV missing, pairing code absent, or controls doing nothing? Check the right connection problem on Android TV and Google TV before changing settings.
body:
# Android TV remote app can't find your TV? Start here

Start with what you can see. A TV that never appears in the phone app needs a different check from one that pairs successfully but won't accept a search. Before changing anything, turn on the TV, check that you're looking at the right TV or streaming-device input, and confirm its network connection.

Then choose your starting point:

- **No TV listed:** check the device and its network
- **TV listed, pairing incomplete:** check the selected screen and pairing code
- **Paired, but an action fails:** test navigation separately from typing, volume, or playback

These checks focus on compatible Android TV and Google TV devices. The pairing instructions below are for Google's Google TV phone app; other apps can use different screens.

## If your TV never appears

### Check what you're trying to control

Find the TV or streaming device's model in its settings, manual, or product label, then check the manufacturer's specifications for its platform. A familiar TV brand or a working YouTube app doesn't identify the operating system.

Google documents its phone remote for Android TV and Google TV. Its separate streaming-device guide names Chromecast with Google TV and Google TV Streamer. An older Cast-only Chromecast shouldn't be treated as the same device. [Google's supported remote setup](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/11221499?hl=en)

If you use a streaming box, check that box's connection as well as the TV. The screen can be on while the box you're trying to control is off or showing on another input.

### Compare the actual connections

Open the phone's Wi-Fi settings and the TV's network settings. For the documented Wi-Fi setup, both should use the same network. On Google TV, Google directs you to **Settings → Network & Internet**. Menu names on other devices can differ. [Google's network check](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/15766805?hl=en)

Check these details before blaming the app:

- Is the phone using mobile data while the TV uses home Wi-Fi?
- Did one device join a guest network?
- Does the TV still remember a network from your previous home?
- If the TV uses Ethernet, does its cable lead to the home network your phone uses? Record that wired setup when asking for help; the Wi-Fi-only instructions don't establish compatibility for every Ethernet configuration

A video loading on both devices proves they can reach the internet. It doesn't prove they can reach each other locally.

Different Wi-Fi bands aren't an automatic diagnosis. Google notes that most routers let devices on 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz communicate. Check the network arrangement before changing bands. [Google's explanation of cross-band communication](https://support.google.com/googlenest/answer/10634602?hl=en-SG)

### Know when the network needs its owner

Guest, hotel, school, and managed networks may separate connected devices. Google documents client-isolation and web-sign-in limitations for its streaming devices. If you're on someone else's network, ask its owner whether local device communication is supported. Keep router security settings intact while you establish the cause. [Google's streaming-device network guidance](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/7566322?hl=en-CA)

If the TV hasn't joined the network at all, restore that connection first using its original remote or a control route supported by the manufacturer.

## If the TV appears but won't pair

In the Google TV phone app, choose your TV from the TV connection button. Enter the code on that screen and tap **Pair**. Google’s Android TV guide labels it **Connect TV**. [Google's pairing instructions](https://support.google.com/androidtv/answer/6122465?hl=en)

**No code visible?** Check the selected device name against the screen in front of you. With several TVs or a plugged-in streamer, it's easy to look at the wrong display or input. Return to device selection and try the intended device again.

**Code rejected?** Use the code currently on that screen. If pairing restarts, don't keep entering a code you copied from an earlier attempt.

Seeing a device in a Cast menu or seeing media controls in Google Home isn't enough to establish that a full remote pairing has completed. Use the remote's pairing flow as your check.

## If it pairs but something doesn't work

Try moving the selection, then Back or Home. Watch whether the TV responds.

If navigation works, write down the action that fails. Test typing in the intended search field with a harmless phrase. If it fails only in one TV app, report that app and field rather than describing the entire connection as broken.

For volume, note whether sound comes from the TV, a receiver, or a soundbar. Google's guidance explains that the streaming device and external audio equipment can have separate volume settings. A working navigation control doesn't settle the audio path. [Google's volume-control guidance](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/10094150?hl=en)

## Try a supported restart, then collect the useful details

If the basic checks don't help, restart the TV or streamer using its official instructions. Google TV provides **Settings → System → Restart** where that menu is available. Let any active software update finish first. [Google TV restart guidance](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/10070482?hl=en)

Afterward, reopen the phone app and retry once. For support, collect:

- Phone model, Android version, and remote-app version
- TV or streamer model and software version
- Wi-Fi or Ethernet connection, including whether it's a guest network
- The exact failure stage and which controls still work
- What changed before the problem started and what you've already tried

Leave passwords and account details out of screenshots. This is more useful than a list of resets that changed several things at once.

## Trying The Remote

The Remote is a free Android phone app for compatible Android TV and Google TV devices. It uses your home network and requires Android TV Remote Service v2; controls vary by model.

[Download the app](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#download) on your Android phone. It's free, with no ads and no account. Before installing, check that your TV is compatible and on the same home network as your phone.
summary: Find the failure stage before pairing everything again.

title: How to type on Android TV with your phone
description: Use your Android phone to type on Android TV or Google TV. Pair the remote, try a text field, and troubleshoot a missing keyboard or text that won’t appear.
body:
# How to type on Android TV with your phone

You can use the Google TV app on an Android phone to enter text on a compatible Android TV or Google TV. Pair the phone with the TV, open a text field on the TV, then try the phone keyboard. Google supports phone-based text entry, but a working direction pad alone doesn’t tell you whether a particular app’s search field will accept it. [Google’s remote features](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/11136134?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en)

Start with a short search. Once you can see those letters arrive, type the long title.

## Connect the phone first

Put the phone and TV on the same home Wi-Fi, with the TV switched on. This route is for Android TV and Google TV. [Android TV setup requirements](https://support.google.com/androidtv/answer/6122465?hl=en)

Open the Google TV app, choose your TV from the connection button, enter the code on the TV and tap **Pair**. Google’s Android TV guide labels it **Connect TV**. [Google’s pairing guide](https://support.google.com/androidtv/answer/6122465?hl=en)

Before going further, use a direction button and watch the TV highlight move. If you have more than one TV, this is also a useful check that you selected the right one.

## Try one short search

Use the remote controls to open the TV app you want, move to its search field and select it. Look for an active text-entry field, rather than leaving the search icon highlighted.

When the phone offers its keyboard, enter a short word such as “jazz”. If your remote screen has a keyboard control, open it. Watch the TV: did the text arrive in the intended field? If it did, finish the query and use the available search or submit control.

If that field ignores the phone keyboard, use the checks below to find out whether the problem follows the field or the whole connection. [Google’s phone-keyboard guidance](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/11221499?hl=en)

## If the keyboard is missing

First, select the TV’s text field again. A page containing a search box isn’t the same as a box ready to receive text.

If you opened the remote from Android’s Quick Settings, try opening the Google TV app itself. Choose the same TV and revisit the same field. Google supports both entry points, so this gives you another way to reach the remote. [Google’s remote entry points](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/11221499?hl=en)

Keep the TV app and search field unchanged during this comparison. Otherwise, you won’t know whether the difference came from the phone’s remote screen or the TV app.

## If the keyboard appears but nothing arrives

Try the same short word in a second TV app’s text field. Then compare the results:

- **Typing works in one field:** you’ve found a working text-entry route. Note which app or field failed; don’t start changing the router because of that one result.
- **Typing fails in both, but navigation works:** record the two failures separately from the working direction controls. That is more useful for support than “the remote doesn’t work”.
- **Navigation also fails:** go back to the connection check. Confirm the selected TV and network before investigating individual apps.

For an unresponsive connection, Google recommends a TV restart: unplug, wait ten seconds, reconnect, then pair again. Let software updates finish first, and check that nobody is watching. [Google’s virtual-remote troubleshooting](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/15766805?hl=en)

## Still stuck? Capture the useful details

Write down the phone model, Android version, TV or streamer model, remote app version, and the exact TV app and field that failed. Include whether the keyboard was missing, whether letters appeared, and whether navigation still worked. Use a harmless sample query in any screenshot.

For Google TV app feedback, open your profile picture, choose **Help & feedback**, then **Send feedback**. Review what you’re sending and keep passwords out of the report. [Google’s feedback instructions](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/9654581?hl=en)

## A phone-first option

With The Remote, you can search YouTube from your phone: type the query on your Android phone and send it to YouTube on a selected compatible Android TV or Google TV over your home network. Its phone typing is for YouTube search only; for other TV apps, use the methods above. It requires Android TV Remote Service v2; whether the TV accepts the search depends on the device and its YouTube version. [The Remote’s compatibility and search details](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#compatibility)

[Download the app](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#download) on your Android phone. It's free, with no ads and no account. Before installing, check that your TV is compatible and on the same home network as your phone.
summary: Get the right letters into the right search field.

title: Search YouTube on your TV with your Android phone
description: Type a YouTube query on your Android phone. Choose between browsing results on the TV, selecting a video on your phone and The Remote.
body:
# Search YouTube on your TV with your Android phone

You have two useful routes: enter text into YouTube’s TV search with a compatible phone remote, or find a video in the YouTube phone app and send that video to the TV. Choose based on where you want to browse the results.

A query such as “live jazz” leaves the next choice open. A video you’ve already selected gives the TV something specific to play.

## Browse the results on the TV

Google’s remote supports text entry on Android TV and Google TV. Whether it reaches YouTube’s search field depends on that field accepting the input. [Google’s remote features](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/11136134?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en)

1. Pair the Google TV phone app using the code on your TV. For this Wi-Fi setup, both devices need the same home network. [Google’s pairing guide](https://support.google.com/androidtv/answer/6122465?hl=en)
2. Open YouTube on the TV and select its search field. The field needs to be active, rather than the search icon merely highlighted.
3. If the phone remote offers its keyboard, enter a short query such as “jazz”. Watch for the letters on the TV.
4. If they arrive correctly, submit the search and use the remote to browse the TV’s results.

If navigation works but the text doesn’t arrive, try another TV app’s search field. A second working field is a useful clue that the first app handles input differently. Keep those results separate when asking for support; “YouTube ignores typed text” is more useful than “nothing works”.

You can use the phone-side route below while you investigate. Repeatedly pairing the same TV is unlikely to tell you more once navigation already works.

## Choose the video on your phone

On the same Wi-Fi, open YouTube on both devices. Search on your phone, select a video, then use **Cast** in its player to choose the TV. Android 17 and later also require YouTube’s local-device discovery permission. [YouTube’s Android casting instructions](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/7640706?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en)

This route suits a particular episode, tutorial or music video you want to inspect on the phone first. Check the title and channel before sending it, especially when several videos have similar names. If other people are using the TV, check the destination before you interrupt their video.

If the TV is missing from the Cast list, YouTube also offers [TV-code linking](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/7640706?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en). You’ll need access to YouTube’s settings on the TV to obtain its code.

## Search while something is already playing

YouTube’s same-account companion experience lets you look for another video on the phone while the TV keeps playing. Its September 2026 update removed the shared-Wi-Fi and manual-connection requirements for that experience. Sign into the same Google Account on both devices. [TeamYouTube’s companion announcement](https://support.google.com/youtube/thread/463959026/use-your-phone-as-a-companion-for-watching-youtube-on-tv?hl=en)

That is a YouTube feature. A separate local-network remote still needs its own connection to the TV. Keep that distinction in mind if YouTube can see a screen that another remote app can’t find.

## The Remote: start with the query

The Remote includes a dedicated YouTube search entered with your Android phone keyboard and sent to your selected TV over the local network. It is for compatible Android TV and Google TV devices with Android TV Remote Service v2. The TV model and YouTube version determine whether the action is accepted. [The Remote’s requirements](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#compatibility)

The [phone-side search walkthrough](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#search-proof) shows where you enter the query. If a query doesn’t arrive on your TV, check the selected destination, then try a search directly in the TV’s YouTube app. If that also fails, resolve the TV-side issue first. If YouTube works but the remote query fails, record the TV model, YouTube version and a harmless sample query for support.

[Download the app](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#download) on your Android phone. It's free, with no ads and no account. Before installing, check that your TV is compatible and on the same home network as your phone.
summary: Choose where you want to browse the results.

title: Open a YouTube link on Android TV from your phone
description: Already have a YouTube link? Open it on your TV with YouTube’s connection options or review the link and pick the TV in The Remote for Android.
body:
# Open a YouTube link on Android TV from your phone

If you already have the video’s link, open it in the YouTube app on your Android phone and connect to the TV. The Remote offers another route for compatible Android TV and Google TV devices: share the link, review the destination, then choose the **Open** action for your selected TV.

You don’t need to type the title into the TV and hunt for the same video again.

## Use YouTube for a link you already have

Open the link in YouTube’s Android app, with YouTube open on the TV and both devices on the same Wi-Fi. Tap **Cast** in the video player and choose the TV. Mobile-browser YouTube doesn’t support this route; Android 17 and later need local-device discovery permission. [YouTube’s Android casting instructions](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/7640706?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en)

For different networks, use YouTube’s TV code: display it under **Settings → Add a device** on the TV, then enter it through **Cast → Add a device** on the phone. Tap **Link** and select the device. [YouTube’s code-linking guide](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/7640706?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en)

Check the title and destination before sending it. You’ll need an existing way to open the TV’s settings for the code route, so it isn’t a shortcut around an unconfigured or unreachable TV.

## Use The Remote’s share-and-review route

This route is for people who already have The Remote installed. You need an Android phone, a compatible Android TV or Google TV device with Android TV Remote Service v2, and a paired TV reachable on your local network. YouTube behaviour depends on the TV and its YouTube version. [The Remote’s requirements](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#compatibility)

### Share one video

Use the Android sharing option for the video or its link and choose The Remote. The share control’s location depends on whether you start in YouTube, a browser or a messaging app.

Share the video link itself. If a conversation contains several videos, choose the one you want first; a screenshot or whole conversation doesn’t identify the destination video reliably.

### Check the link and the screen

Review the link and selected TV in The Remote. If you’ve saved several TVs, pick the room where you want to watch. Check that another person isn’t using that screen before you send anything.

If you copied the link from a conversation, check it against the original message before continuing.

### Open it on the selected TV

When the link and destination are right, tap the **Open** action for that TV. The action sends the supported YouTube link to the selected compatible device.

Check the TV for the result. Its YouTube app, signed-in account and the video’s availability still determine playback. Your phone’s account, captions and playback position may not carry over.

## If it stops along the way

**The TV isn’t available:** check the saved destination and home-network connection. If the TV still remembers an old Wi-Fi network, restore its connection before trying again.

**The shared item isn’t accepted:** open the original video in the YouTube phone app and use the connection route above. URL formats can differ: a working ordinary video link doesn’t establish that Shorts, playlists or timestamp parameters behave the same way.

**YouTube opens but the video doesn’t play:** read the message on the TV. A sign-in request, unavailable video or playback error needs resolving there before sending the link again.

**The wrong TV received it:** check that screen before retrying elsewhere. Correct the selected destination before the next **Open** action.

## Give the link a destination

A shared video deserves a quick check before it reaches a bigger screen. The Remote keeps that choice explicit: review the link, choose the TV, then send it.

[Download the app](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#download) on your Android phone. It's free, with no ads and no account. Before installing, check that your TV is compatible and on the same home network as your phone.
summary: Give a video you already found the right destination.

title: Lost your Android TV remote? What works before buying another
description: Lost your Android TV remote? Try a phone remote, check the old-Wi-Fi trap, and find safe, model-specific options before buying a replacement.
body:
# Lost your Android TV remote? What works before buying another

If your Android TV or Google TV is already connected to your home network, try the Google TV app on your Android phone. If the TV still remembers an old Wi-Fi network, or is waiting for first-time setup, a local-network remote app may not be able to reach it. Start with the branch that matches your screen.

## First, check whether your remote can ring

Have a Google TV Streamer and its paired Google TV Streamer Voice Remote? Briefly press the button on the back of the Streamer. The remote should sound for 30 seconds. Press any button on the remote once you find it. This button method is specific to the Streamer and its paired Streamer Voice Remote. Follow Google's [Find My Remote instructions](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/15322770?hl=en-GB), and don't hold the button down.

## The TV is already on your home network

Use Google's phone remote first:

1. Turn on the TV. For a separate streamer, select its HDMI input.
2. On the same home Wi-Fi, open the Google TV phone app and choose the TV from its connection button.
3. Enter the TV’s code, tap **Pair**, then try moving the TV selection.

See [Google’s pairing instructions](https://support.google.com/androidtv/answer/6122465?hl=en) if the app’s labels differ.

If the TV doesn't appear, check the simple things before changing settings: is the TV awake, and is your phone on the usual home Wi-Fi rather than mobile data or a guest network? If you can already see the TV's network status, compare it with your phone's connection.

For an unresponsive Google TV, unplug it for 10 seconds, reconnect, then retry pairing. Follow any different manufacturer instructions and let updates finish first. See [Google's virtual-remote troubleshooting](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/15766805?hl=en).

### Both devices have internet, but they still can't connect

Internet access doesn't prove the devices can reach each other locally. Guest and managed networks may separate devices. Google identifies client isolation and sign-in-page networks as problems for its streaming devices. On a hotel, office or shared network, ask the owner which connection supports your device. Don't disable network security to make a remote app work. [Google's network guidance](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/7566322?hl=en-CA)

## You moved home or changed the Wi-Fi

This is the awkward loop: the TV needs a controller to join the new network, while your phone needs a reachable TV before it can act as that controller. Installing more local-network remote apps won't connect the TV to the new Wi-Fi for you.

Look for a control route that doesn't depend on that connection:

- **Buttons on the TV.** Check your model's manual for the power button or control panel and what it can operate. Some controls offer more than power; others don't. Sony's [remote troubleshooting guide](https://www.sony.com/electronics/support/articles/00030297) includes checking the TV's own buttons.
- **The television's remote, if you lost a streaming-box remote.** If HDMI-CEC control is supported and already configured, the TV remote may operate the connected device. Check both manuals. Sony calls its implementation [BRAVIA Sync](https://helpguide.sony.net/tv/nusltn1/v1/en-003/print.html); that example doesn't establish support for every TV-and-box combination.
- **A USB keyboard you already own.** Check the manufacturer's accessory guidance before trying it. Sony says many USB keyboards are recognised by its Google TV and Android TV models, while warning that functions can vary. That's a possible route on supported hardware, not a guarantee of full menu control. [Sony keyboard guidance](https://www.sony.com/electronics/support/articles/00128141)

Once one of these controls works, use the TV's network settings to join your current home Wi-Fi, then retry phone pairing. On Google TV, look under **Settings → Network & Internet**, as described in [Google's connection checks](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/15766805?hl=en).

Ethernet may also be an option when the device has a supported port or adapter and can join your home network. For example, Google documents [Ethernet for its streaming devices](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/10109908?hl=en). A cable doesn't guarantee that phone pairing or unfinished setup will work. Check the exact hardware before buying an adapter.

## The TV is on a setup screen

Follow the instructions for that model and the screen you're actually seeing. Google offers [phone-assisted setup on supported Google TV devices](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/10050221?hl=en), but its setup sequence can still require a paired remote before the phone takes over. A QR code setup option and an everyday phone remote are different stages.

Avoid a factory reset as a lost-remote shortcut. Google warns that resetting its streaming devices erases data and cannot be undone. You may end up back at setup with the same missing controller. [Google's reset warning](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/6254654/how-to-factory-reset-your-chromecast-android?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en-SG)

If none of the supported routes is available, borrow or buy a remote confirmed for the exact model. Check the model label on the TV or streaming box, then use the manufacturer's replacement and pairing guidance. A matching brand name alone isn't enough.

## Set up a backup while you have control

Once the TV is reachable again, pair your phone and check the controls you rely on. Keep the physical remote available for setup and any functions your phone can't operate.

Want to try The Remote as another phone-control option? It's for Android phones and [compatible Android TV or Google TV devices](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#compatibility) on the local network. [Download the app](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#download) on your Android phone. It's free, with no ads and no account. Before installing, check that your TV is compatible and on the same home network as your phone. Use an available rescue route above if you are stuck today.
summary: Recover control based on your TV’s network and setup state.

title: Is there an app to search YouTube on my TV from my phone?
description: Yes. The Remote is a free Android app that lets you type a YouTube search on your phone, and the results open in YouTube on your Android TV or Google TV. No ads, no account.
body:
# Is there an app to search YouTube on my TV from my phone?

Yes. The Remote is a free Android app that lets you type a YouTube search on your phone, and the results open in YouTube on your Android TV or Google TV. It has no ads and no account.

## Type the search on your phone, and the results open on the TV

1. Open The Remote and pick the TV.
2. Tap Search YouTube.
3. Type your search on your phone keyboard and send it.
4. The results open in YouTube on the TV, where everyone in the room can see them.

The first time, the TV may ask which app to use. Choose YouTube.

## Results on the TV are different from casting a video

When you cast, you pick the video on your phone, and only that video goes to the TV. With a search, the results grid opens on the TV, so the room can choose together. If you already know the video, sharing its link works better: see [how to send a YouTube link to your TV](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/guides/app-to-send-youtube-link-to-tv/).

## YouTube also has its own phone options

YouTube's phone app can cast to the TV, link to it with a TV code, and act as a companion while you watch, including voice search. [YouTube Help: watch on your TV](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/7640706?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en) These work well if you want to browse on your phone first.

## What you need

- An Android phone with Android 8.0 or later. There's no iPhone version.
- An Android TV or Google TV with Android TV Remote Service v2, on the same home Wi-Fi as your phone.
- YouTube on the TV. Search support depends on the TV's YouTube app version.

The Remote's phone typing is for YouTube search only. It doesn't type into other TV apps.

## Where The Remote fits

The Remote is a free phone remote for Android TV and Google TV. Search YouTube from your phone, share a YouTube link and it plays on the TV, and keep your TVs organised by room. No ads, no account.

[Download the app](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#download)
summary: Type the search on your phone. The results open on the TV.

title: Is there an app that sends a YouTube link to my TV?
description: Yes. Share a YouTube link to The Remote on your Android phone, pick the TV, and it plays on your Android TV or Google TV. Works with links from YouTube, WhatsApp or a browser.
body:
# Is there an app that sends a YouTube link to my TV?

Yes. On your Android phone, share a YouTube link to The Remote, pick the TV, and it plays on your Android TV or Google TV. It works with a link you found in YouTube, got in WhatsApp or opened in a browser. The Remote is free, with no ads and no account.

## Share the link to The Remote, then pick the TV

1. Tap Share on the video or the link, in YouTube, WhatsApp, a browser or another app.
2. Choose The Remote from the share list.
3. Check the link and pick the TV, like Living room or Bedroom.
4. Tap Open on that TV. The video plays on the TV.

The TV may still need you to confirm playback.

## It works for links someone sent you

The usual route, casting, starts from the YouTube app. A shared link skips the search: if a friend sends a video in a chat, share it straight to The Remote and pick the TV.

## Pick the right TV first

If you've saved more than one TV, check which one is selected before you open the link. That way it plays on the screen you meant, not on the one someone else is watching. See [remote apps for multiple TVs in different rooms](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/guides/tv-remote-app-for-multiple-tvs-in-different-rooms/).

## If it doesn't open

Open YouTube on the TV, make sure it's up to date, and try again. Link support depends on the TV and its YouTube app version. If the TV shows a message, sort that out on the TV first. The [open-a-link guide](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/guides/open-youtube-link-on-android-tv/) covers YouTube's own casting and TV-code options too.

## What you need

An Android phone with Android 8.0 or later (no iPhone version), and an Android TV or Google TV with Android TV Remote Service v2 on the same home Wi-Fi.

[Download the app](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#download)
summary: Share the link to The Remote, pick the TV, and it plays there.

title: How do I check if my TV has Android TV Remote Service?
description: On the TV, open Settings, then Apps, then See all apps, show system apps, and look for Android TV Remote Service. If it's listed and enabled, phone remotes can connect.
body:
# How do I check if my TV has Android TV Remote Service?

Open your TV's Settings, go to Apps, then See all apps, turn on Show system apps, and look for Android TV Remote Service. If it's listed and enabled, phone remote apps can connect to the TV over your home Wi-Fi.

## Find it in the TV's system apps

1. On the TV, open **Settings**.
2. Go to **Apps**, then **See all apps**.
3. Choose **Show system apps**.
4. Scroll to **Android TV Remote Service** and open it.

Menu names vary by brand and model, so the steps may look a little different. The service is built into Android TV and Google TV and doesn't show up on the home screen. [Android TV Remote Service listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.tv.remote.service&hl=en)

## Make sure it's enabled

On the service's page, check that it isn't disabled. If someone turned it off, phone remotes can't pair. If you can't find it at all, your device may not run Android TV or Google TV: see [how to tell if your TV is Android TV or Google TV](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/guides/is-my-tv-android-tv-or-google-tv/).

## If it's there but pairing still fails

Start with the network. The phone and TV must be on the same home Wi-Fi, not a guest network, and the TV must be on. The [can't-find-your-TV guide](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/guides/android-tv-remote-app-cant-find-tv/) walks through the checks in order.

## What The Remote needs

The Remote needs Android TV Remote Service v2 on the TV. It works with Google TV devices that support the Android TV Remote Service, including Chromecast with Google TV and Google TV Streamer. [Google Streaming Help](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/11221499?hl=en) Your phone needs Android 8.0 or later (no iPhone version). Here's [what Android TV Remote Service is](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/guides/what-is-android-tv-remote-service/).

[Download the app](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#download)
summary: Find the service in your TV's system apps and check it's enabled.

title: Does an Android TV remote app work on a Fire TV Stick?
description: No, not apps built for Android TV and Google TV. Fire TV runs Amazon's Fire OS. Use Amazon's Fire TV app as a phone remote instead. The Remote doesn't support Fire TV.
body:
# Does an Android TV remote app work on a Fire TV Stick?

Remote apps built for Android TV and Google TV, including The Remote, don't work with Fire TV. Fire TV Sticks and Fire TV Edition TVs run Amazon's Fire OS, not Google TV. Use Amazon's own Fire TV app on your phone instead.

## Fire TV runs Fire OS, not Google TV

Fire OS is Amazon's own system. It doesn't have the Android TV Remote Service that Android TV and Google TV phone remotes connect to. So a remote app made for Google TV won't find a Fire TV Stick or pair with it. Home Assistant's Android TV Remote documentation makes the same point. [Home Assistant: Android TV Remote](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/androidtv_remote/)

That includes TVs with Fire TV built in, sold under other brands. If the home screen says Fire TV, this applies.

## Amazon's Fire TV app is the phone remote for Fire TV

Amazon makes a free Fire TV app for Android and iPhone. Put your phone on the same Wi-Fi as the Fire TV, open the app, pick your device, and type the code shown on the TV. Its listing says it needs an Amazon account. [Amazon Fire TV app](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.amazon.storm.lightning.client.aosp&hl=en_IN)

If your router uses advanced settings, Amazon's guide says multicast support needs to be on for the app to connect. [Amazon Fire TV user guide (PDF)](https://d1ergij2b6wmg5.cloudfront.net/Amazon+Fire+TV+User+Guides/Amazon+Fire+TV+Device+Documentation/Amazon_Fire_TV_User_Guide.pdf)

## The Remote is for Android TV and Google TV only

The Remote works with Android TV and Google TV devices that support Android TV Remote Service v2. It doesn't support Fire TV, Roku or Apple TV, and there's no iPhone version.

## Not sure which one you have?

Check the home screen and the settings menu. Here's [how to tell if your TV is Android TV or Google TV](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/guides/is-my-tv-android-tv-or-google-tv/).

If you also have a Google TV or Android TV in the house, The Remote is a free phone remote for it, with no ads and no account. [Download the app](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#download)
summary: Fire TV runs Fire OS, so use Amazon's app. The Remote doesn't support it.

Google's help pages say you can use the Google Home app or the Google TV app as a phone remote for Chromecast with Google TV and Google TV Streamer. [Google Streaming Help](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/11221499?hl=en) It suits homes that already use Google Home for other devices.

## Your TV maker's app

Some TV makers have their own remote apps. Sony's BRAVIA Connect controls supported BRAVIA TVs and Sony home-theatre products from your phone. Sony lists the supported models, and says the app needs your Google Account signed in on the TV. [Sony: BRAVIA Connect or Google TV app](https://www.sony.com/electronics/support/articles/00347983) Check your TV maker's support site for its own app.

The Remote is free, with no ads, no account and no sign-up. It adds:

- YouTube search typed on your phone, with the results opening on the TV

It's Android only (Android 8.0 or later) and installs from our website. Your TV needs Android TV Remote Service v2. That includes Google TV devices that support the Android TV Remote Service, such as Chromecast with Google TV and Google TV Streamer. YouTube support depends on the TV's YouTube app version. For a closer comparison, see [Google TV app vs The Remote](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/guides/google-tv-app-vs-the-remote/).

## Not an alternative: apps for other systems

Fire TV, Roku, Samsung and LG TVs have their own remote apps. Android TV remotes, including The Remote, don't control them. See [the Fire TV answer](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/guides/does-android-tv-remote-app-work-on-fire-tv-stick/).

title: Google TV app vs The Remote: which phone remote should I use?
description: Both are free phone remotes for Android TV and Google TV that pair with the code on your TV. Google's app types into any text box that accepts it. The Remote adds no account, YouTube search from your phone, link sending, TVs by room and Guest mode.
body:
# Google TV app vs The Remote: which phone remote should I use?

Both are free phone remotes for Android TV and Google TV, and both pair with the code your TV shows. Use Google's Google TV app if you want Google's official remote, with phone typing in any text box that accepts it. Use The Remote if you want a remote with no account and no ads, plus YouTube search from your phone, YouTube links that play on the TV, TVs organised by room and a Guest mode. Many people keep both.

## What Google's Google TV app does

According to Google, the Google TV app's remote can play and control media, turn the TV on or off, use Google Assistant, change the volume, and enter text for searches or login details. You pair it by choosing the TV and entering the code it shows, on the same Wi-Fi. Android users can add the remote to Quick Settings. [Google TV Help](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/11136134?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en) It's also available on iPhone. [Google Streaming Help](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/11221499?hl=en)

## What The Remote adds

- **No account and no ads.** No sign-up, no sign-in, no in-app purchases.
- **YouTube search from your phone.** Type the search on your phone, and the results open in YouTube on the TV.
- **YouTube links that play on the TV.** Share a link to The Remote, pick the TV, and it plays there.
- **TVs organised by room.** Name each TV and give it a room, like Living Room TV or Bedroom.
- **Guest mode.** Limits the remote to navigation, play/pause and volume. Hold the TV name for 1 second to exit.
- **Layout options.** Larger controls, Easy remote, home-screen widgets and app language options.

## Side by side

- **Price:** both free. The Remote has no ads.
- **Pairing:** both use the code on the TV and need the same Wi-Fi.
- **Typing:** Google's app enters text in text boxes that accept it, including logins. The Remote's phone typing is for YouTube search only.
- **YouTube:** in Google's app, you type into YouTube's search box on the TV. The Remote has its own YouTube search and YouTube link sharing.
- **Several TVs:** The Remote names TVs and sorts them by room.
- **Phones:** Google's app runs on Android and iPhone. The Remote is Android only (Android 8.0 or later).
- **How you get it:** Google's app comes from app stores. The Remote installs from our website.

## Typing on the TV

Need to type a Wi-Fi password, a login or a search in an app other than YouTube? Use the Google TV app. Searching YouTube is where The Remote helps: some users find YouTube's TV search box doesn't take phone-keyboard text, and The Remote has its own YouTube search. See [why your phone keyboard may not type in YouTube](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/guides/why-wont-my-phone-keyboard-type-in-youtube-on-android-tv/).

## If you lost your remote

Both work as a backup remote when the TV is already on your home Wi-Fi. Neither can reach a TV that's off the network or still on a setup screen. The [lost remote guide](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/guides/lost-android-tv-remote/) covers those cases.

## Which TVs

The Remote works with Android TV and Google TV devices with Android TV Remote Service v2. That includes Google TV devices that support the Android TV Remote Service, such as Chromecast with Google TV and Google TV Streamer. [Google Streaming Help](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/11221499?hl=en) Controls vary by model. YouTube support depends on the TV's YouTube app version.

[Download the app](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#download)
summary: What each one does, side by side, with sources.

title: How can guests control my Google TV without a Google account?
description: Chromecast's old guest mode is gone, so guests now join your Wi-Fi to cast. A guest with an Android phone can also use The Remote, with no account, after pairing with the code your TV shows. The Remote also has a Guest mode.
body:
# How can guests control my Google TV without a Google account?

Guests need your Wi-Fi. Google has dropped Chromecast's guest mode, so guests now join your Wi-Fi to cast. A guest with an Android phone can also use The Remote, which needs no account. They join your Wi-Fi and enter the code your TV shows. The Remote also has its own Guest mode, which limits the remote to navigation, play/pause and volume.

## Chromecast guest mode is no longer supported

Google's help page says it plainly: "Guest mode is no longer supported. Guests can cast content from their Android or iOS devices by connecting to the host's Wi-Fi network." [Google: guest mode](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/6109286) That old feature let people cast to older Chromecasts without joining your Wi-Fi. It ended in 2023, and it was never part of Chromecast with Google TV. [9to5Google](https://9to5google.com/2023/08/23/chromecast-guest-mode/)

## Guests can cast once they're on your Wi-Fi

To cast from YouTube or another Cast-enabled app, a guest's phone has to be on the same Wi-Fi as the TV. That's Google's own advice above.

## A guest can use The Remote with no account

The Remote doesn't ask anyone to sign up or sign in. A guest with an Android phone (Android 8.0 or later) joins your home Wi-Fi, installs The Remote from our site, picks the TV and enters the code it shows.

## The Remote's Guest mode limits the remote to the basics

The Remote has a Guest mode. When it's on, the remote is limited to navigation, play/pause and volume, and the screen says "Guest mode is on". To exit, hold the TV name at the top for 1 second.

## Where The Remote fits

The Remote is a free phone remote for Android TV and Google TV devices with Android TV Remote Service v2. That includes Google TV devices that support the Android TV Remote Service, such as Chromecast with Google TV and Google TV Streamer. No ads, no account. There's no iPhone version.

[Download the app](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#download)
summary: What replaced Chromecast guest mode, and what The Remote's Guest mode does.

title: How do I install an Android app from a website instead of Google Play?
description: Download the APK on your phone, open it and tap Install. Android asks once to allow installs from your browser, and you can turn that off again afterwards.
body:
# How do I install an Android app from a website instead of Google Play?

Download the app's APK file on your Android phone, open it, and tap Install. The first time, Android asks you to allow installs from the app you downloaded with, usually your browser. Allow it, install, then turn that setting off again if you like.

## The four steps

1. Tap the download button on your Android phone.
2. If Android asks, allow installs from your browser.
3. Open the downloaded file and tap Install.
4. Open the app.

## Android asks once for permission to install from your browser

Android blocks installs from outside an app store until you allow them for a specific app, like Chrome or your file manager. The prompt takes you straight to the switch. You can turn it off again after installing.

## Only install APKs from the developer's own site

Download the file only from the developer's official page. Android checks the app's signature before installing it. Some developers also publish a SHA-256 checksum so you can confirm the file matches what they released.

## Updating means downloading the new version from the same page

An app installed this way doesn't update through an app store. Download the latest version from the same page and open it. Android installs it over your current app when the version and signing match. If Android refuses, keep the app you have and check the file came from the right page. Uninstalling first removes the app's saved data.

## The Remote installs this way

The Remote isn't on Google Play. You download it from our website and install it on your phone in the steps above. The download section on our home page shows the current version, file size and SHA-256 checksum. Once it's installed, pick your TV and enter the code it shows.

The Remote is a free phone remote for Android TV and Google TV, with no ads and no account. It needs Android 8.0 or later. There's no iPhone version.

[Download the app](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#download)
summary: Download, allow installs from your browser once, open, install.

title: How do I know if my TV is Android TV or Google TV?
description: Open Settings, then System (or Device Preferences), then About. If you see an Android TV OS version, it runs Android TV or Google TV. The home screen tells you which one.
body:
# How do I know if my TV is Android TV or Google TV?

Open the TV's Settings, go to System (or Device Preferences), then About. If you see an "Android TV OS" version, your TV runs Android TV or Google TV. To tell them apart, look at the home screen: Google TV shows Google TV branding and your Google account icon, and Android TV shows a simpler layout.

## Look for "Android TV OS" in Settings

Sony documents the check for its TVs: **Settings → System → About → Android TV OS version**. Older models list it under About → Version. [Sony: which Android version is on my TV?](https://www.sony.com/electronics/support/articles/00115311) Other brands use similar menus, so the exact names may differ.

If you can't find any Android TV OS version, your TV probably runs a different system, like Samsung's Tizen, LG's webOS, Roku or Fire TV.

## The home screen tells Google TV from Android TV

Google TV is the newer interface, and it runs on Android TV OS. On Google TV, the home screen shows Google TV branding and a profile icon for your Google account. Android TV typically shows a clock or settings icon in that spot instead. [Sony: Google TV, Android TV or other?](https://www.sony.com/electronics/support/articles/00200248)

For a phone remote, both count. Apps made for Android TV work on Google TV too.

## The brand on the TV doesn't tell you

Many brands sell Google TV models next to models with other systems. Two TVs from the same brand can run different software. Check the settings, not the logo.

## If a streaming box gives you the home screen, check the box

If your home screen comes from a box or stick plugged into the TV, the box is what your phone remote talks to. The Remote works with Google TV devices that support the Android TV Remote Service, including Chromecast with Google TV and Google TV Streamer. [Google's streaming-device remote guide](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/11221499?hl=en) A Fire TV Stick runs Fire OS, not Google TV: see [the Fire TV answer](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/guides/does-android-tv-remote-app-work-on-fire-tv-stick/).

## One more check for The Remote

The Remote works with Android TV and Google TV devices that support Android TV Remote Service v2. Here's [what Android TV Remote Service is](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/guides/what-is-android-tv-remote-service/). Available controls vary by model and firmware.

It's free for Android phones (Android 8.0 or later), with no ads and no account. [Download the app](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#download)
summary: Find "Android TV OS" in Settings, then read the home screen.

title: Can I use my phone as a TV remote without Wi-Fi?
description: Wi-Fi phone remotes, including The Remote and Google's app, need your phone and TV on the same network. Without Wi-Fi you need an IR blaster or a Bluetooth route your TV supports.
body:
# Can I use my phone as a TV remote without Wi-Fi?

Only with the right hardware. Most phone remote apps for Android TV and Google TV, including The Remote and Google's Google TV app, work over Wi-Fi, so your phone and TV have to be on the same network. Without Wi-Fi, you need a phone with an infrared (IR) blaster, or a Bluetooth connection your TV supports.

## Wi-Fi remotes need your phone and TV on the same network

Google's own phone remote says it plainly: your phone and TV must be on the same Wi-Fi network. [Google's virtual-remote checks](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/15766805?hl=en) Internet on both devices isn't enough. They have to be able to reach each other on the local network.

## An IR blaster works without Wi-Fi, if your phone has one

A few phones have an infrared emitter, like a classic remote. With an IR remote app and the right profile for your TV, they can send basic commands with no network at all. Most phones don't have one, so check your phone's specs first.

## Bluetooth is another route on some TVs

Some apps connect to Android TV over Bluetooth as a remote or keyboard. Whether it works depends on the TV, and setup usually starts in the TV's remotes and accessories settings, which means you need a way to reach that menu first.

## Guest, hotel and office Wi-Fi often block phone remotes

Even when there is Wi-Fi, networks that keep devices apart (client isolation) or need a sign-in page can stop a phone from finding the TV. On someone else's network, ask the owner. Don't switch off security settings. [Google's network guidance](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/7566322?hl=en-CA)

## The TV lost its Wi-Fi and you have no remote

That's the awkward loop: the TV needs a remote to rejoin Wi-Fi, and a Wi-Fi remote needs the TV on Wi-Fi. The [lost remote guide](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/guides/lost-android-tv-remote/) covers the ways out: buttons on the TV, HDMI-CEC and a USB keyboard.

## The Remote needs your home Wi-Fi

The Remote is a Wi-Fi remote. Your Android phone (Android 8.0 or later) and your Android TV or Google TV (with Android TV Remote Service v2) need to be on the same home Wi-Fi. It's free, with no ads and no account.

[Download the app](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#download)
summary: Wi-Fi remotes need a shared network. IR and Bluetooth are the exceptions.

title: What is the code my TV shows when I pair my phone?
description: It's a short-lived pairing code that proves the phone in your hand may control that TV. Type the code that's on screen now.
body:
# What is the code my TV shows when I pair my phone?

It's a pairing code. Your Android TV or Google TV shows it so only someone looking at the screen can connect a phone to it. Type the code from the TV into your phone app, and the phone is paired. The code can include letters, so copy it exactly.

## Type the code that's on the screen right now

Pairing codes only last a short time. If pairing restarts, the TV shows a new code. Use the one on the screen now, not one from an earlier try. Google's pairing steps work the same way: choose the TV, enter the code it displays, tap Pair. [Google's pairing guide](https://support.google.com/androidtv/answer/6122465?hl=en)

## No code on the screen usually means the wrong TV is selected

If no code appears, check that the TV you picked in the app is the one in front of you. With two TVs, or a streaming box on another HDMI input, it's easy to send the request to a screen you aren't looking at.

Also check the TV is on and on the same home Wi-Fi as your phone.

## In The Remote, you enter the code when you add a TV

Pick your TV in The Remote and enter the code it shows. Then the TV is saved in your list with the name and room you gave it.

## After a TV update, you may be asked again

If a TV update resets the connection, The Remote may ask you to pair again. Let the update finish, turn the TV on, check it's on the same Wi-Fi, then enter the new code shown on the TV.

## It's a code, not a password

You don't make it up and you don't need to remember it. There's no account behind it either: The Remote doesn't ask you to sign in.

[Download the app](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#download) on your Android phone (Android 8.0 or later). It works with Android TV and Google TV devices that support Android TV Remote Service v2. There's no iPhone version.
summary: What the pairing code is, why it times out, and when you'll see it again.

The name lives in the app. You don't need to rename the TV in its own settings.

## Each TV pairs with its own code

## Every TV needs to be on your home Wi-Fi

Your phone talks to each TV over your home network. A TV on a guest network, or one that still remembers an old Wi-Fi, won't show up until it's on the same network as your phone. If a TV goes missing, the [can't-find-your-TV guide](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/guides/android-tv-remote-app-cant-find-tv/) helps.

Android TV and Google TV devices with Android TV Remote Service v2, including Google TV devices that support the Android TV Remote Service, such as Chromecast with Google TV and Google TV Streamer. Available controls vary by model and firmware. Not sure what yours runs? See [how to tell if your TV is Android TV or Google TV](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/guides/is-my-tv-android-tv-or-google-tv/).

# Can I use a TV remote app without an account?

Amazon's Fire TV app, for example, says on its listing that it needs an Amazon account. Check any remote app's listing if you'd rather not sign in. [Amazon Fire TV app listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.amazon.storm.lightning.client.aosp&hl=en_IN)

title: What is Android TV Remote Service?
description: Android TV Remote Service is a system app built into Android TV and Google TV that lets a phone act as the remote over Wi-Fi. The Remote needs version 2 of it.
body:
# What is Android TV Remote Service?

Android TV Remote Service is a system app built into Android TV and Google TV. It lets a phone act as the TV's remote over your home Wi-Fi, with navigation, typing and more. Wi-Fi phone remote apps, including Google's Google TV app and The Remote, connect to it. The Remote needs the newer version, Android TV Remote Service v2.

## It's the part of your TV that listens for a phone remote

When you pair a phone, this service shows the pairing code on the TV and then accepts commands from the paired phone. Google describes it as the service that lets you use your phone or tablet as a remote. [Android TV Remote Service listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.tv.remote.service&hl=en)

## You don't install it: it comes with the TV

It's preinstalled on Android TV and Google TV devices and updates like the TV's other system apps. You won't find it on the home screen. It's listed among system apps in Settings.

## The Remote needs Android TV Remote Service v2

The service has had more than one version. The Remote needs Android TV Remote Service v2. If your TV doesn't support it, The Remote can't pair with it. The Remote also works with Google TV devices that support the Android TV Remote Service, including Chromecast with Google TV and Google TV Streamer. [Google's streaming-device remote guide](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/11221499?hl=en)

## How to see it on your TV

On most Android TV and Google TV models: **Settings → Apps → See all apps**, then show system apps and look for **Android TV Remote Service**. Its page shows the installed version. Menu names vary by brand.

## Fire TV, Roku and other TVs don't have it

Only Android TV and Google TV include this service. That's why phone remotes built on it don't work with Fire TV, Roku, Samsung (Tizen) or LG (webOS). See [does an Android TV remote app work on a Fire TV Stick?](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/guides/does-android-tv-remote-app-work-on-fire-tv-stick/)

## Where The Remote fits

The Remote is a free phone remote for Android TV and Google TV devices with Android TV Remote Service v2. Search YouTube by typing on your phone and the results open on the TV. Share a YouTube link and it plays on the TV. No ads, no account. Your phone needs Android 8.0 or later.

[Download the app](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#download)
summary: The built-in part of your TV that a phone remote connects to.

title: Why won't my phone keyboard type in YouTube on Android TV?
description: Phone remotes type into whatever text box the TV has selected, and YouTube's TV search doesn't always accept that text. Here's what to check, and a phone-typed YouTube search that opens results on the TV.
body:
# Why won't my phone keyboard type in YouTube on Android TV?

A phone remote types by sending letters to whichever text box is active on the TV. On some TVs, YouTube's search box doesn't accept that text, so you end up back on the on-screen letter grid. Check the TV's keyboard setting first. Or use The Remote, a free Android app with its own YouTube search: you type on your phone, and the results open on the TV.

## Phone keyboards type into the box the TV has selected

Google's Google TV app can type on Android TV and Google TV with your phone's keyboard. It only works once a text box on the TV is selected and ready for text. [Google's remote features](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/11221499?hl=en)

That works well in the TV's own search, Wi-Fi passwords and many apps. It depends on each app's search box accepting the text.

## YouTube's TV search doesn't always take that text

Reviewers and users have reported for years that YouTube on Android TV handles its search differently from a standard text box, so phone typing may not reach it. [Android Police on the Android TV remote](https://www.androidpolice.com/2021/09/27/hands-on-how-to-android-tv-new-remote/)

If typing works in the TV's main search but not in YouTube, your phone and TV are fine. The difference is in the YouTube box.

## Check the TV's keyboard is Gboard first

On many Google TV models, phone typing relies on Gboard being the TV's keyboard. Open **Settings → System → Keyboard → Current keyboard** and pick Gboard. Menu names vary by TV. [Google TV community answer](https://support.google.com/googletv/thread/377486628/where-is-keyboard-option?hl=en)

Then:

1. Select YouTube's search box on the TV, not just the search icon
2. Type a short word like "jazz" on your phone
3. Watch the TV. If no letters arrive, try the TV's main search to compare

If you plugged in a USB keyboard or its receiver, unplug it. Some TVs hide the on-screen keyboard while one is connected. [Sony's keyboard note](https://www.sony.co.uk/electronics/support/articles/00133802)

## The Remote has its own YouTube search, and the results open on the TV

In The Remote, tap Search YouTube, type on your phone keyboard and send it to the TV you picked. The results open in YouTube on that TV.

Search support depends on your TV and its YouTube app version. If a search doesn't open, update YouTube on the TV and try again.

## Typing in other TV apps still needs another remote

The Remote's phone typing is for YouTube search only. For passwords, Wi-Fi or other apps' search boxes, use Google's Google TV app or the TV's own keyboard. The [typing guide](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/guides/type-on-android-tv-with-phone/) walks through it.

## Where The Remote fits

The Remote is a free phone remote for Android TV and Google TV. No ads, no account. You need an Android phone (Android 8.0 or later; there's no iPhone version) and a TV with Android TV Remote Service v2, on the same home Wi-Fi. [Download the app](https://theremote-site.pages.dev/#download)
summary: Why YouTube's TV search can ignore your phone keyboard, and what works instead.
